title: Artificial intelligence-based identification of octenidine as a Bcl-xL inhibitor.
summary: Deep-learning and docking screening nominated octenidine as a Bcl-xL binder. The abstract reports NMR binding, reduced intracellular Bcl-xL/Bak interaction and cancer-cell effects; full-text methods and quantitative assay details were not assessed.
ai_technology: Structural-feature-based deep learning plus molecular docking
organization: Korea Research Institute of Bioscience and Biotechnology; Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Korea University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports NMR binding to the Bcl-xL BH3-binding region, NanoBiT inhibition of Bcl-xL/Bak-BH3 interaction in cells, and apoptosis-associated proliferation inhibition in MCF-7 and H1299 cells. Denominators and quantitative potency were not stated in the reviewed abstract.
evidence.unknown: Only the PubMed abstract and metadata were reviewed. Full-text methods, concentrations, denominators, quantitative binding data and detailed controls were not assessed; cell results do not establish treatment efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: The primary abstract reports structural-feature-based deep learning and molecular docking to screen an approved-drug library; architecture, training data and candidate denominator were not assessable from the abstract.

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed abstract and bibliographic metadata only; full text not reviewed.
